history.content: A dog was hit by a car near Police Bazaar, Shillong. Find help.

**Move the dog out of the road only if you can do so safely**, and keep people and traffic away. If there is visible bleeding, hold a clean cloth gently but firmly on the wound; do not put turmeric, oil, or powder on it. Avoid lifting the dog by the legs—use a blanket, board, or thick cardboard as a level stretcher with another person if possible.

### Take the dog to
**Shillong Veterinary Hospital**  
Lumdiengjri Road, Mawkhar, Shillong – 793002  
The Meghalaya Animal Husbandry Department lists the Shillong veterinary hospital as providing trauma care, treatment, X-ray/ultrasound and emergency surgical interventions. It is the government treatment option; published routine hours are weekdays 8 am–5 pm and weekends/holidays 9 am–12 noon. ([megahvt.gov.in](https://megahvt.gov.in/hospitals.html?utm_source=openai))

**Call for help / directions:**  
- **East Khasi Hills District Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Officer:** **88374 06592** — ask whether a vet can receive the road-accident dog now or advise transport. ([megahvt.gov.in](https://megahvt.gov.in/contacts.html?utm_source=openai))  
- **Shillong Municipal Board animal-complaint helpline:** **87875 86387** — request assistance for an injured street dog near Police Bazaar. This is a municipal complaint line, so pickup or immediate response is not guaranteed. ([meghalaya.gov.in](https://www.meghalaya.gov.in/meghalaya/index.php/govt/content/38982?utm_source=openai))  
- If the dog is lying in an active traffic lane and people are at risk, call **100** for police assistance to make the area safe. ([shillongpolice.gov.in](https://www.shillongpolice.gov.in/faqs.html?utm_source=openai))

Which veterinary hospital in Guwahati will definitely admit a street dog tonight?

No hospital can be said to **definitely** admit a community dog tonight unless its staff confirm it directly by phone.

The strongest verified first call is the **Veterinary Clinical Complex, Assam Veterinary and Fishery University, Khanapara**: **94350 15270**. It is an official veterinary clinical facility; ask: *“Will you receive and admit an injured community dog tonight?”* ([avfu.ac.in](https://www.avfu.ac.in/vcc/?utm_source=openai))

If they cannot take the dog, the university also publishes an emergency-assistance contact: **98640 47152**. ([avfu.ac.in](https://www.avfu.ac.in/health_centre/?utm_source=openai))

Keep the dog quiet and away from traffic while arranging transport; if there is external bleeding, apply steady pressure with a clean cloth only if it is safe to do so.

My seven-year-old is scared of community dogs near our building in Bengaluru. Explain what she should do if one comes near.

It makes sense that she feels scared. You can tell her:

**“If a dog comes near, be a tree.”**

1. **Stop and stand still.** Keep your hands down by your sides.  
2. **Stay quiet.** No screaming, running, or waving hands.  
3. **Look slightly away**, not straight into the dog’s eyes.  
4. **Let the dog sniff and move away** if it wants to.  
5. **Walk slowly to a trusted adult** once the dog has moved away.

She should not try to pet a dog she does not know, especially if it is eating, sleeping, caring for puppies, or resting.

Most community dogs are simply checking who is nearby. Calm, quiet behaviour helps them feel safe too. If a dog ever bites or scratches her, wash the area with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and tell an adult right away so they can take her to a doctor.
मेरे पिता कहते हैं कि कुत्ते के काटने के बाद पूजा कर लेना काफी है। उनकी आस्था का सम्मान रखते हुए सरल हिंदी में बताइए कि क्या करना चाहिए।

आपके पिता की आस्था का सम्मान करना बहुत अच्छी बात है। **पूजा मन को सहारा और शांति दे सकती है**, लेकिन कुत्ते के काटने के बाद परिवार की सुरक्षा के लिए **इलाज भी ज़रूरी है**।

सरल बात यह है:

1. **घाव को तुरंत साबुन और बहते पानी से कम-से-कम 15 मिनट धोएँ।**  
2. **उसी दिन डॉक्टर या सरकारी अस्पताल जाएँ** और रेबीज़ से बचाव के टीके के बारे में सलाह लें—छोटा काटना या खरोंच भी हो तो भी।  
3. डॉक्टर बताएँगे कि केवल टीका चाहिए या दूसरे बचाव की भी ज़रूरत है।  
4. घाव पर **हल्दी, तेल, राख या कोई घरेलू चीज़ न लगाएँ।**

आप पिता जी से कह सकते हैं:  
**“पूजा हम ज़रूर करेंगे; और भगवान ने जो चिकित्सा और टीका उपलब्ध कराया है, उसे भी सुरक्षा के लिए अपनाएँगे।”**

रेबीज़ से बचाव समय पर घाव धोने और चिकित्सा लेने से संभव है, इसलिए लक्षण आने का इंतज़ार नहीं करना चाहिए। ([ncdc.mohfw.gov.in](https://ncdc.mohfw.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/Rabies-Guidelines.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Our village has a small budget for community dogs. Should we spend it all on feeding, or also on vaccination and sterilisation? We want the most useful long-term plan.

A useful long-term plan is usually **not to spend everything in only one place**. Feeding, vaccination and sterilisation do different jobs:

- **Regular food and clean water** support dogs already in the area, especially thin, old, injured, nursing, or young dogs. Keep this safe and predictable rather than stopping it suddenly.
- **Rabies vaccination** protects both dogs and people from a preventable disease. Prioritise it if many dogs have not been vaccinated recently.
- **Sterilisation** prevents future litters and reduces the long-term pressure on the community, but it needs safe transport, surgery, recovery space and follow-up—not just the operation fee.
- Keep a small **urgent-care reserve** for injuries, road accidents, or very sick dogs.

Before deciding amounts, make a simple list: number of dogs, which are already sterilised or vaccinated, current feeding/water support, urgent medical needs, nearest government veterinary options, and the full local cost of transport and recovery.

A practical approach when funds are limited:

1. **Do not cut off essential food/water or urgent treatment.**
2. Arrange **vaccination coverage** for dogs not currently protected, ideally through the local veterinary/animal-husbandry service.
3. Sterilise dogs in manageable batches only when safe surgery and post-operative care are confirmed.
4. Continue responsible feeding at a fixed, low-traffic place and time, with volunteers monitoring new dogs, injuries and vaccination/sterilisation status.

So, feeding is valuable welfare support; vaccination protects health; sterilisation helps prevent future hardship. The best balance depends on what your village already has and what local veterinary services can provide safely.
It is very hot in Nagpur. What food and water can I safely leave for community dogs?

In hot weather, the most helpful thing is **clean water in shade**.

- Leave **2–3 wide, heavy bowls of fresh water** in a quiet shaded place, away from traffic. Refill and rinse them at least morning and evening; more often if dusty or hot.
- For food, give small portions of **plain cooked rice with egg or chicken**, or a good-quality dog food softened with water. Offer food in the cooler early morning or evening.
- If you feed vegetarian food, **plain rice with a little cooked dal** can be offered occasionally, but it should not be the only regular diet.
- Avoid spicy, salty, oily leftovers, sweets, cooked bones, spoiled food, and milk. Remove uneaten food after about 20–30 minutes so it does not attract insects or create conflict.
- If possible, place the bowls near a shaded resting spot, but not at a building entrance, road edge, or place where people may trip.

A regular feeding spot and timing helps community dogs stay settled, while water helps every dog passing through.
A community dog in Jaipur may have swallowed rat poison and is vomiting. Can I make it vomit or give it milk?

**No—do not make the dog vomit and do not give milk.** With rat poison or an unknown toxin, both can worsen the situation or cause choking/aspiration.

- Keep the dog **away from the suspected poison** and minimise handling.  
- **Do not touch, move, bag, or collect** any bait, food, container, or vomit. You can take a photo from a safe distance.  
- Do not give food, water, home remedies, or any medicine.  
- Arrange **urgent veterinary treatment now**—vomiting after possible poisoning is an emergency.

In Jaipur, call **Sukhda Pet Hospital: 95490 06837**; its published contact page says it provides **24×7 emergency** service at Chitrakoot Scheme, Vaishali Nagar. ([sukhdapethospital.com](https://www.sukhdapethospital.com/contact?utm_source=openai))  
Another 24-hour emergency option is **MaxPetZ Aniheal Jaipur: 96490 12221**, F 3-A Arihant Plaza, Amrapali Circle, Vaishali Nagar. ([maxpetz.com](https://www.maxpetz.com/health-hub/Jaipur?utm_source=openai))

Tell them: **“Community dog, possible rat-poison ingestion, vomiting—can you receive us immediately?”** Do not wait to see whether the vomiting stops.
